title: Supplier acceptance timeline & compatibility review - Stellar Commerce kickoff
summary: Introductory procurement + technical compatibility call to align MSA/DPA expectations, KMS/egress constraints, SLA targets, and pricing path for a short pilot. Customer emphasized data residency and auditability; Redwood clarified hosted vs Dedicated options and can provide a pilot with limited data set and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share redlines, security pack, pilot scope doc, and schedule a bench test with a small dataset.
topics: SLA latencies and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-26
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor, Priya Shah, Noah Patel, Rita Gomez, Samir Desai (Stellar Commerce)
Shared links: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (reference), pricing-worksheet-v2.xlsx (Redwood), pilot-scope-draft.md (link)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy): Align on MSA/DPA exceptions, KMS integration approach, and pilot scope. Confirm timeline for procurement and technical preflight.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and this is Carlos our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Liam O'Connor: Good thanks, Liam here. We got a few folks from legal and engineering on so we can move fast.
[00:10] Priya Shah: Hi, Priya from legal, quick note, we'll want to close DPA items and a few MSA clauses up front.
[00:15] Carlos Ruiz: Totally, understood. We'll try to surface the typical exceptions we see.
[00:18] Noah Patel: Quick ask from my side — we need to confirm data residency and KMS keying model; we can't have provider-managed keys for production.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Yup, that's expected. Redwood has a Private deployment path and Dedicated with customer KMS options — we can map that out.
[00:32] Rita Gomez: For the pilot, we just want to validate throughput and p99 latency at about 200 qps with 1k token average; is that feasible on Hosted?
[00:42] Carlos Ruiz: Hosted might hit cost/latency tradeoffs at that scale, we'd likely recommend Dedicated or a small reserved pool for deterministic p99. For pilot we can emulate with a burstable dedicated node.
[00:53] Samir Desai: On pricing, procurement wants committed pricing bands; we need visibility into data egress and KMS charges.
[00:59] Jordan Lee: We have a pricing worksheet that shows egress, per-token, and dedicated hourly reserve rates — I'll share that after the call.
[01:10] Priya Shah: MSA — two items: indemnity cap and data return/deletion language. Can you confirm standard retention windows and audit log availability?
[01:20] Maya Chen: Standard hosted retention is 30 days for non-enterprise, but for enterprise we can set retention per contract; audit logs are available and we can provide access to request logs and token-level traces. We'll include a SOC2 summary in the security pack.
[01:35] Priya Shah: We'll need the SOC2 type II report and an attestation for subprocessor list. Also, clarify whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys.
[01:45] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, customer-managed keys via KMS are supported on Dedicated and Private deployments; HSM integrations are available for Private deployments. For Hosted we can offer a bring-your-key path for certain enterprise tiers — we should tie that to the contractual commitments.
[01:58] Noah Patel: Good. On the technical side, what about model variants and fallbacks — we need automatic graceful degradation if primary model capacity is saturated.
[02:06] Carlos Ruiz: Smart routing handles that — policies can fallback to compatible quantized variants or different regions. For the pilot we can set a hard capacity threshold and an automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper lower-capacity model to preserve availability.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: Timeline question: procurement has a monthly gating window on the 15th for legal signoff. If we want production by end of Q2, what's the ideal timeline?
[02:31] Maya Chen: If procurement signs off in early March, we can run a 2-3 week pilot in March, finalize MSA/DPA in parallel and aim for Dedicated capacity spin-up in April, then staging in May and production end of June — that aligns with your Q2 target but depends on KMS/HSM approvals.
[02:48] Priya Shah: On DPA redlines, we have some standard clauses around breach notification and data subprocessor flow-down; we may ask for a 30 day notification window for subprocessor changes.
[02:58] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll mark those and provide our standard flow-down and a subprocessor list.
[03:05] Rita Gomez: A couple engineering specifics: we use private VPCs in GCP and we need to understand egress patterns, NAT, and peering. Also want to test prefix/KV cache behavior for our prompt families.
[03:18] Carlos Ruiz: For VPC peering we support VPC peering and private connectivity; we'll send a technical preflight checklist. Regarding KV cache, we can enable prefix caching and show hit rates during the pilot — that's usually a big cost saver.
[03:30] Samir Desai: Anything in the contract about billing reconciliation if latency targets not met? We want credits or service deductions.
[03:37] Jordan Lee: SLA credits are included in enterprise SLAs; we can map latency SLOs to credits. Need to agree on measurement windows — e.g., monthly p95 and p99 targets.
[03:47] Priya Shah: Can you also confirm export controls and whether Redwood exports data out of region for model updates? That affects our data residency stance.
[03:56] Maya Chen: Generally, model training pipelines are separate; inference logs and customer data are not exported without contractual agreement. We can restrict routing to a region and provide egress maps. We'll add a data residency annex.
[04:08] Noah Patel: For pilot success criteria, I propose: 1) p99 <= 600ms for 1k token avg at 200 qps sustained for 10 minutes, 2) KV cache hit >= 40%, 3) KMS integration verified with rotation, 4) no unexpected data egress.
[04:22] Carlos Ruiz: Those are measurable; we'll try to instrument exact counters and attach dashboards in the pilot scope doc.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: From procurement: our tolerance for vendor lock-in is medium; we need clear termination/transition assistance language and data export mechanics.
[04:37] Priya Shah: Also escrow options for model artifacts?
[04:40] Maya Chen: We can discuss transitional support and export mechanics; escrow for customer-specific artifacts can be arranged for enterprise deals.
[04:48] Rita Gomez: Technical follow-ups — can Carlos share a list of required ports and ip ranges for the preflight? We prefer minimal outbound egress.
[04:55] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, I'll include ports, CIDR blocks, and peering notes in the preflight checklist.
[05:02] (murmurs)
[05:10] Jordan Lee: Pricing note — if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity at X units, we can drop per-token price by 15% and include a KMS pass-through credit; details in the worksheet.
[05:22] Samir Desai: That sounds interesting; what's the minimum commit?
[05:25] Jordan Lee: Typically we look for a baseline monthly commit that maps to sustained throughput — I'll propose three tiers in the worksheet so procurement can choose.
[05:33] Priya Shah: Back to the MSA, we may need to negotiate indemnity in certain jurisdictions — can you provide preferred alternatives?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Yes, our legal team has standard fallbacks; I'll include alternatives when I send the annotated MSA.
[05:47] Liam O'Connor: Ideally we close procurement gates by March 15th so we can begin pilot in late March. Is that realistic?
[05:55] Maya Chen: It's tight but doable if we get quick redlines this week. We'll prioritize the security pack and MSA/DPA.
[06:03] Priya Shah: We'll aim to return redlines by 2025-03-03; if there are complex exceptions it might slide but we'll try.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Great, we'll run concurrent threads: legal and security while Carlos and Rita set the pilot preflight.
[06:17] Rita Gomez: One more thing — we use customer-side HSM for key rotation and need rotation cadence to be compatible with our SIEM ingest times.
[06:25] Carlos Ruiz: We support configurable rotation windows and can provide rotation hooks to your SIEM; we'll add that to the preflight.
[06:32] (brief silence)
[06:36] Maya Chen: OK, let's recap next steps — we'll send MSA/DPA redlines and the security pack, Carlos will send the pilot plan and preflight checklist, Jordan will send pricing tiers, and Liam will circulate procurement timeline.
[06:50] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:53] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the links and schedule the bench test.
[06:58] Priya Shah: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-heard words and speaker labeling may be off; timestamps approximate.
